top_issues.issue: World hue collapses at mid depth; every world's mid layer is the same neutral grey/black
top_issues.why: Violates 'one hue per world': three mid-depth frames are interchangeable, and deep CRYOS/MAELIS drift to teal and navy, which belong to other worlds.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep a per-world hue floor in the rock albedo and the lit/shadow tint at every depth (amber-brown, ice-blue, sea-green/nacre) and vary value and saturation by depth, not hue. Deep CRYOS should go toward deeper blue/cyan, not green.

top_issues.issue: Fissures are flat stick decals that emit no light
top_issues.why: The reference's key read is fissures that branch and light the stone around them. Here they are small disconnected T/Y glyphs on unlit black cubes.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make continuous branching vein paths that cross block boundaries, add emissive bloom, and add a warm vertex or emissive falloff on the faces next to a vein so the stone near a fissure glows.

top_issues.issue: Liquid/hot blocks are flat, unlit, opaque colour
top_issues.why: The orange/green pools read as UI rectangles. They neither bloom nor wash the adjacent rock, so 'light lands' fails, and the CRYOS pool is matte sage rather than glowing cyan.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make them emissive with a brighter core and softer edges, add bloom, and spill their colour onto the neighbouring rock faces. Use per-world liquid colours (molten amber, cyan, sea-green brine).

top_issues.issue: Rock reads as a uniform tile grid, not cubic faceted stone
top_issues.why: The 03 reference has chunky cubes with varied sizes, offsets and facet tones, and a lit face distinct from a black face. These frames are equal squares with near-identical value, so they look flat.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add per-block jitter (small offsets and scale, a bevelled or chipped facet or two) and per-face tone variation, and push top/side face value contrast where the lamp hits. Keep it low-poly; this is not texture work.

top_issues.issue: Excavated cave interiors are a dead flat backdrop with no depth or haze
top_issues.why: The back wall is a uniform rectangle of dim squares with a hard frame edge, so there is no midground/background separation and the dug space looks like a box.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Darken the back wall and give it a world-hued haze, plus a little geometric relief, so it sits clearly behind the play-layer rock while the lamp still grazes it.

top_issues.issue: Emissives don't bloom and their light doesn't land on surfaces. Lava, fissures, ore and crystals render as flat unlit colour or thin decals.
top_issues.why: These break rules 1 and 2 of the brief (Glow, Light lands). References 03 and 04 hinge on ore and fissures glowing into the dark and lighting the stone around them.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Push emissive intensity above the bloom threshold and add a soft bloom pass. Give lava pools and fissure clusters cheap local point lights (or baked vertex light on neighbouring faces) so the adjacent rock picks up their hue. Draw fissures as glowing strokes with a halo, not 1px lines.

top_issues.issue: The headlamp is a radial glow, not a beam. Nothing visible in the air, no dust, no directional cone.
top_issues.why: Reference 03 is the closest target and its signature is a visible beam with dust in it that lights the faces it hits. Right now the lamp only lights an evenly filled box around the pod.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add an additive volumetric cone mesh (gradient falloff) along the drill direction, plus drifting dust motes inside it. Make the lamp a spotlight so hit faces are bright and side faces fall off to black, instead of a near-uniform fill on the cavity walls.

top_issues.issue: The three worlds aren't separated by hue underground, and the core hues look off-brief.
top_issues.why: Rule 4 (one hue per world): the CRYOS and MAELIS mid-depth frames are nearly indistinguishable from each other and from VEIL. The CRYOS core reads green and the MAELIS core reads violet-blue, which inverts the ice-cyan / sea-green targets.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tint the lamp, the cavity fill/fog and the rock albedo per world: cold blue-white lamp and cyan fill for CRYOS, green-teal fill and iridescent highlights for MAELIS. Recheck the core colours: CRYOS should be ice-cyan, MAELIS sea-green/nacre.

top_issues.issue: The core lights itself but doesn't flood its chamber.
top_issues.why: Reference 07 is about the core washing the whole chamber in light. Here the floor, the pillars and the left wall stay near-black, so it reads as a bright sprite in a dark room rather than a sacred light source.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Put a strong large-radius light at the core position in the core hue, add a warm/cool haze gradient that brightens toward it, and rim-light the pillars and floor tops on the core-facing side. Keep the far side dark for contrast.

top_issues.issue: No haze or depth layering. The surface/title frames are evenly lit, and underground the background reads as a flat box.
top_issues.why: Rule 3 (Depth) asks for value and haze separation, with black kept for true void. The title should sell the descent (01-title), but instead it shows a bright surface vista with no glow from below.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add distance fog/haze tinted to the dusk on the surface so the domes and sun recede. For the title, consider framing or overlaying a dark shaft with a warm up-glow. Underground, give back walls a faint cooler haze so they separate from foreground blocks without flattening the dark.

top_issues.issue: Mid-depth band (464m) has no world identity at all
top_issues.why: All three mids are the same near-black neutral grey rock under a warm lamp. The brief says a screenshot from any depth should say which world it is, and these fail completely.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Carry each world's hue through its mid band: tint the rock albedo and the darkest fill or fog toward the world hue (amber, ice-blue, sea-green), and give the mid band its own world-coloured emissive accent (veins, crystals, growth) so the hue is present without flattening the dark.

top_issues.issue: CRYOS deep/core and MAELIS deep/core hues are swapped
top_issues.why: CRYOS turns teal-green at depth and MAELIS turns navy/violet, so the deep frames of each world read as the other world. That directly contradicts 'one hue per world' and the 05/06 references.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep CRYOS on ice-cyan/blue at every depth (cyan fissures, pale cyan-white heart) and MAELIS on sea-green/nacre (green-teal fissures, a pearl with an iridescent sheen over green light). Each world should hold its hue through every band; the bands should vary value and saturation, not hue family.

top_issues.issue: Liquid pools are flat, unlit, and the same green in two worlds
top_issues.why: The pool is the biggest emissive area in each frame, yet it's a flat opaque slab of identical green in CRYOS and MAELIS, so it erases the distinction between those worlds and doesn't glow onto the stone around it.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each world its own pool colour (CRYOS glowing cyan, MAELIS brine sea-green, VEIL molten orange) with soft bloom and light spilling onto the adjacent blocks.

top_issues.issue: Lamp and cavity fill are warm amber in every world
top_issues.why: The same warm sodium wash fills the cavity in all three worlds and pulls the cold worlds toward brown and olive. In the cavity, the largest open area of each frame, the world hue gets overridden.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the headlamp near-white, and let the cavity's air or haze and the bounce light take the world tint (cool cyan haze in CRYOS, green brine haze in MAELIS, amber dust in VEIL), so the beam stays readable while the space around it says which world it is.

top_issues.issue: Fissures and veins are decals that don't light the stone
top_issues.why: Per 04-veil-deep, the fissures should carry world identity by washing the rock around them in the world hue. Here they are thin lines on dark blocks, so the hue stays a pattern rather than an atmosphere.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a soft glow halo and a tint on the faces next to each fissure in the world hue, so deep bands are saturated with their world's colour while true void stays black.

top_issues.issue: Fluid pools are flat, unlit, opaque colour blocks
top_issues.why: References 04/05/06 make the pool the brightest, glowing light source that washes nearby rock. Here the pools read as solid tiles with no surface, depth or emission, which breaks both 'Glow' and 'Light lands'.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make pool surfaces emissive with a brighter top surface or meniscus line and a slight gradient with depth, add soft bloom, and place a coloured point/area light per pool (or a vertex-light pass) so adjacent block faces pick up the pool hue. Keep it faceted and low-poly.

top_issues.issue: Fissures are decal glyphs that neither glow nor light their stone
top_issues.why: The art direction asks for fissures that branch and light the stone around them (04). Short disconnected tick marks read as scratches or UI noise, and the blocks they sit on stay as dark as everything else.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make the fissures continuous branching paths that cross block boundaries, give them an emissive core with a softer bloom falloff, and add a local glow or tint on the block faces they cross (falloff a block or two out). Use fewer, longer, brighter veins instead of many tiny marks.

top_issues.issue: World hue is wrong or muddled for CRYOS and MAELIS
top_issues.why: CRYOS-2 should be ice-cyan/blue but the pools, fissures and core are mint/emerald green. MAELIS-6 should be sea-green/nacre but its rock, fissures and pearl are lavender/blue. So a frame can't tell you which world it is.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Push CRYOS pools, fissures and the heart to a saturated cyan (around #4fe0ff) on cold blue rock. Give MAELIS a sea-green/teal brine with a subtle iridescent pink-violet sheen on the pearl and rock highlights, and keep the base hue green-teal rather than violet.

top_issues.issue: Core chambers aren't flooded with light; core is cropped and the space reads as void
top_issues.why: Ref 07 has the core lighting the whole chamber: walls, floor and the small figure. Here the core sits half off-screen, the far walls and ceiling stay black, and a black band under the floor makes the chamber feel unfinished, not sacred.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Frame the core fully in view at arrival, or reveal it as the camera pans in. Give it a strong wide-falloff light that rims chamber walls, pillars and floor in the world hue. Add a visible chamber back wall in a lifted, hazy version of the core colour, and fill or shade the void under the floor.

top_issues.issue: Pools and fissures have no interaction with the dark or the lamp
top_issues.why: Darkness is the medium. Emissives should be the islands of information in it, but these pools look identical whether or not the lamp is near, and they have no specular response.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a specular or Fresnel highlight on the pool surface where the headlamp hits, plus a faint shimmer or slow emissive pulse. Keep the surrounding rock dark so the pool's own light is what reveals its edges.

top_issues.issue: Creatures do not glow or light their surroundings
top_issues.why: The reference's core promise is creatures whose light spills onto the rock. Here every creature is an unlit flat-colour mesh, so the fauna adds nothing to the theme that light is gameplay
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each species an emissive part (glimmerfly bodies, shellback bulbs, stillwalker joints or tips) in a per-world hue, with a soft additive halo sprite and a small point light or light-decal on nearby blocks. Swarm glimmerflies into a sinuous ribbon with tapering density

top_issues.issue: The pod doesn't match the chunky faceted white design
top_issues.why: A smooth glossy ball with a dark green-black visor loses the faceted low-poly identity and the bright teal visor that should be the player's beacon in the dark
top_issues.suggested_direction: Rebuild the hull as a blocky panelled white body (flat-shaded, a few bevelled plates) with chunky legs and a drill arm. Make the visor a bright emissive teal with bloom so it reads at 60px

top_issues.issue: Pilot lacks orange trim and a glowing visor
top_issues.why: The trim is the pilot's accent colour and the glowing visor makes the figure findable in dark vaults; without them the pilot is a plain white figure
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add orange collar, cuffs and boots and a backpack, and make the visor emissive teal with a small bloom. Consider a slightly larger head-to-body ratio for readability

top_issues.issue: Creature silhouettes read as props or placeholders
top_issues.why: The shellback reads as a spiked crate, the stillwalker as a dead tree, and the warden as a black block with a lamp. Players can't tell living things from terrain
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each a clear readable creature shape (head, limbs, a shell arc) in chunky faceted low-poly, a lighter value than the background rock, and a rim or emissive edge to separate it from the dark

top_issues.issue: Placeholder black box around the pilot at vault spawn
top_issues.why: The square black frame with green lines sits behind the pilot and kills the warm pool of light the character should stand in
top_issues.suggested_direction: Remove or soften the spawn frame and let the sconce light wash over the pilot and the masonry

top_issues.issue: Vault rooms sit in a black starfield void instead of a cooler, hazier masonry backdrop
top_issues.why: The references separate platforms from a lit, cool blue-grey back wall. Here black is the default background rather than true void, so there's no depth and the place doesn't feel like a stone vault.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a dim back-wall layer of dressed square stone (or a cool blue-grey haze plane) behind the playfield, a few value steps above black and cooler than the foreground. Keep pure black for true pits and voids only.

top_issues.issue: Sconces and lanterns don't pool warm light on the masonry
top_issues.why: Warm pools on stone are the signature of the 08 references and mark the light the player navigates by. Right now the lights are bright points with no wash, and the stone is uniformly flat grey-brown.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each sconce a warm amber point or spot light with a visible falloff halo on nearby wall and floor faces, plus soft bloom on the flame. Let the stone between sconces fall to cool dark.

top_issues.issue: Fang/spike hazards are low contrast against the dark
top_issues.why: The rows of dark red spikes nearly vanish into black, which breaks the 'mood never wins over knowing where to step' rule.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give fangs a brighter emissive tip or rim (hot orange-red) with a faint glow line along the strip, so they stay legible unlit.

top_issues.issue: Room-overview zoom makes play elements unreadable
top_issues.why: At this scale, footing, gates and hazards collapse to specks, and debris clouds (Return, Kindled) read as noise and hide the route.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Cap the overview zoom-out, or boost the outlines and emissives on platforms, gates and hazards when zoomed out. Thin out or dim the floating debris cubes so they sit behind the play layer.

top_issues.issue: Dark silhouette figures and dark platforms merge with the background
top_issues.why: Black-filled shapes with thin violet outlines, and near-black ledges, lose their edges against a black background.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Light platform tops with a lit-edge highlight, or catch them with the headlamp. Push the background up a value step so dark shapes read against it.

top_issues.issue: Title wordmark collides with the scene
top_issues.why: The letters overlap the lit signage and buildings, so neither reads. The title should sell descent and darkness (ref 01), not a bright surface diorama.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Darken or vignette the scene behind the title, or frame the shot so the type sits over sky or void. Consider a slow warm glow under the wordmark and dimmer surface lights. Give the tagline a scrim or more contrast.

top_issues.issue: Panels feel like generic web UI, not diegetic to the world
top_issues.why: The navy rounded card and grey buttons read as a SaaS modal, and the cool slate tone breaks VEIL's one-hue amber rule.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Warm the panel base toward a near-black warm brown or charcoal, use squarer, faceted corners that echo the low-poly rock, give item icons a soft emissive glow, and tint panel chrome per world (amber/cyan/sea-green).

top_issues.issue: HUD lacks glow and doesn't respond to the world's light language
top_issues.why: The brief says every emissive blooms, but the HUD bars and numbers are flat. The lumens currency is also the brightest thing on screen, so it competes with ore and the lamp.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a subtle bloom or soft outer glow to the bars and readouts. Drop the lumens to a quieter weight until it changes. Add a low-fuel or low-hull pulse so the bars carry stakes.

top_issues.issue: Small text and icons at the bottom right are hard to read
top_issues.why: Readability of play is a non-negotiable, and the cargo ore list is tiny and low-contrast against dark rock.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Bump the size a step, add a faint dark scrim behind the cargo stack, and give the ore icons their in-world emissive colour.

top_issues.issue: Ending screen has no light

top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a single faint warm or star-core glow (or a dimming one, to match the 'nothing in the sky' text) behind OUT. Shorten the line length and lift the body text contrast slightly.

per_shot.note: Thirteen hues are mostly distinguishable, but every ore is a tiny flat-shaded decal on a black or orange square: no glow, no host rock, and several silhouettes contradict the brief.
Brown and orange dimpled balls with no verdigris teal crust and no glowing cells. They read as rust or gold nuggets.
Faceted lumpy nodule is roughly the right shape, but it is one brown tone with matte tan patches instead of a teal shell with hot orange cells inside.
Pale grey-white blocks: the opposite of the dark gunmetal brief. Almost identical to rime salt and the pale silver shards.
Cubic cluster silhouette is right, but the flat light-grey unlit material has no blue-black tone and no specular. It reads as chalk.
Tiny white slivers that are hard to see at gameplay size, and the same white shards are scattered as decoration across ordinary rock tiles.
Thin blades are the right idea, but they come out as 1 to 3 loose shards, not a fan spraying out of rock, and they have no metallic edge highlights.
Yellow reads as gold and stands apart from the other ores, but it is a flat mustard crumple with no glow.
Crumpled-foil nugget with no rock outside, no glowing wound and no amber warmth leaking out. It looks like a paper ball.
The only saturated red-pink and instantly identifiable, but the shape is a flat blob with no inner glow or light pooling.
Chunky stubby shape and colour are on brief. Facets are barely shaded, there is no hexagonal crystal read and no glow.
Ovoid purple egg reads, but it is one flat violet with no blue-magenta iridescence. It is hard to tell from the mimic.
Egg silhouette and small facets are right. The colour is a single lavender fill: no rainbow flashes, no base glow, no dark base.
Clean pointed gem, but it is saturated cyan rather than colourless or pale ice, so it competes with veinlight teal and the cyan visor.
Crisp lozenge silhouette, the cleanest shape in the set. Two flat tones, no sparkle and no cool bloom.
Orange four-point stars read as shuriken. Wrong value: it should be a black shard with ember pinpricks, and here it is the brightest warm ore.
Solid orange throwing-star blades: no obsidian body, no sparks, no glowing seams. It collides with gold and copper.
Teal reads as the bio colour, but the shape is a soft blob. Nothing branches and no light spills onto rock.
Rounded teal lumps with no fronds or crystal cluster and no glow lighting the base. It is not a plant.
Distinct from voidopal only by a subtle pink stripe. There is no rock husk and no red-orange crack tell.
A pink band wraps the egg like a planet ring. The tell exists but it is the wrong colour, wrong motif and too faint at gameplay size.
Lavender radial starburst is the most on-brief silhouette, but it is thin and wiry, with no glowing white centre.
Good starburst geometry and lavender hue, but too few, too-sparse points. It reads as a spider or asterisk, not a dense frost flower.
Small white blocks indistinguishable from iron. No glacier blue, no translucency, no cyan light.
Cubic shape is right, but the opaque pale grey material is a copy of iron and lacks the blue translucent inner light.
Small white slivers that look like the silver and quartz debris around them. Effectively invisible as a distinct ore.
Pale lavender-white needle shards: no scalloped shell, no ribbing, no pearl iridescence. It reads as silver.

top_issues.issue: No emissive glow or light spill anywhere; ores are unlit flat colour fills
top_issues.why: The art direction's first rule is that every emissive blooms into the dark and light lands on nearby surfaces. Ore that glows into black rock is the core image of 03-veil-mid, and right now nothing glows.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give glowing ores (copper cells, gold wound, ruby, voidopal, embershard seams, veinlight, frostbloom centre, rime salt) an emissive core plus a soft additive halo sprite or bloom, and a small point or fake light that tints the adjacent rock face. Keep iron, silver and nacre non-emissive and readable by specular instead.

top_issues.issue: Ore tiles render as pure black squares with the mineral floating in them; there is no host rock
top_issues.why: The brief says ore sits on or erupts from matte dark-grey rock. A black void tile reads as a hole or UI icon, cuts the ore off from the world and kills the 'golden wound in rock' (gold) and 'crystals erupting from stone' (silver, ruby, veinlight) shape language.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Render the ore tile as normal host rock (same material and lighting as neighbours) with the mineral embedded or protruding. For gold and mimic, build the rock husk as part of the ore mesh, split open to reveal the glowing interior.

top_issues.issue: Pale ores collapse into one look: iron, rime salt, silver, nacre and the white decorative shards are all flat light grey
top_issues.why: Iron should be the dark blue-black non-glowing cube and rime salt the translucent glacier-blue cube. Nacre should be a ribbed iridescent shell. Today iron and rime salt are the same white blocks, nacre equals silver, and random white shards in plain rock make silver unreadable.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Iron: dark gunmetal (#2a2f3a-ish) with bright blue specular edges. Rime salt: blue translucent cube with frosted white top and cyan inner glow. Nacre: scalloped fan with a pink, teal and violet gradient or vertex-colour sheen. Silver: a denser fan of 5 to 8 needles rooted in a rock base. Remove or darken the white shard decoration on non-ore rock, or make it clearly rock-coloured.

top_issues.issue: Embershard, copper and mimic carry the wrong identity tells
top_issues.why: Embershard is a solid orange star, the brightest warm object, when it should be the darkest: a black shard with ember pinpricks. Copper is brown rather than teal-crust with orange cells. The mimic tell is a faint pink ring rather than red-orange crack lines, so it barely separates from voidopal.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Embershard: jagged black-blue slab mesh with emissive orange seam lines and dot sparks. Copper: teal-green faceted shell with recessed emissive orange cell faces. Mimic: blue-grey cracked rock husk around violet facets, with bright red-orange emissive crack lines across the husk.

top_issues.issue: Gem colour fills are single flat tones with no iridescence or facet value range
top_issues.why: Voidopal's identity is shifting blue, violet and magenta. Diamond should be colourless with sparkle, not saturated cyan, which clashes with veinlight and the visor. Flat fills read as stickers, not faceted low-poly crystal.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use per-face colour variation (vertex colours or a hue-shift by face normal) so facets read light and dark. Give voidopal a blue-to-magenta gradient across faces. Make diamond near-white or pale ice with a strong specular and a twinkle sprite. Make veinlight a branching frond or crystal cluster with a glowing base.
